title: voyage-batch startup: auto-detect and refresh stale Ixdar automation server
description:
Today, after changing Ixdar Java source (a port rename, a node-logic fix, etc.), the developer must manually restart the long-running automation server on port 47832 before voyage-batch picks up the new behaviour. If they forget, validate_dsl in the voyage loop still uses the old in-memory classes even though the catalog, system prompt, and compiled .class files on disk are already up to date. This was hit live in a /be-voyage-agent session where MESH-42 renamed boolean_math's 'mode' input to 'operation'; the catalog + prompt said operation=, the validator said mode=, and the agent had to fall back to the old port name to make progress. The fix was in the compiled classes but invisible at runtime.

Principle: one step should reset everything. The voyage harness (voyage-batch CLI) should take responsibility for ensuring the automation server it talks to is running the currently-compiled code. The developer should never have to remember a 'restart the server' step — that's a step easy to forget and the failure mode (wrong validator behaviour) is silent and confusing.

Proposed approach (startup phase of voyage-batch):
1. Locate the Ixdar checkout (already resolved via resolve_ixdar_root in validate_dsl.py).
2. Determine whether the automation server is running on :47832. Options: port probe via GET /health, or walk pgrep for an Ixdar main class.
3. If running, compare its JVM start time (ps -o lstart, or /proc on linux) against the newest mtime in ixdar-app/target/classes. If any .class is newer than the server started, consider it stale.
4. If stale OR not running: run 'mvn -q -pl annotations,ixdar-app compile' first (ensures target/classes reflect source), then kill the stale process if any, then start a fresh automation server in the background and wait for /health to return 200.
5. If fresh: reuse as-is.
6. Print a one-line status on every voyage-batch start: '[automation] reusing server pid=N (started 14:32)' or '[automation] restarting stale server (compiled classes newer than server start)'.

Optional sweeter design: expose '/version' on the automation server that returns a short hash derived from class file mtimes or a build-id property, so the staleness check doesn't rely on ps/lstart which is platform-quirky. But mtime-based check is fine for macOS/Linux and adds no server-side code.

Big wins: no more silent split-brain between catalog/prompt and validator; no more 'did you restart the server?' debugging step; voyage runs after Java changes Just Work. The related skill files (.claude/skills/be-voyage-agent and ~/Code/Daud README) can drop the 'ensure automation server is running' prereq entirely.
definition-of-done: 1. voyage-batch CLI startup performs the detect-and-refresh sequence before the agent loop begins. 2. Staleness is detected when any file under ixdar-app/target/classes has an mtime newer than the running automation server's start time (getprocess_create_time equivalent). 3. On detected staleness, voyage-batch kills the stale server and starts a fresh one, blocking until /health returns 200. 4. On no server running, voyage-batch compiles if needed and starts one. 5. Status line printed on every startup so the developer can audit what happened. 6. Corresponding skill file (.claude/skills/be-voyage-agent) drops the manual 'ensure server is running' prereq. 7. Failure modes are graceful: if mvn compile fails, voyage-batch prints the build error and exits non-zero; if the server fails to come up, same.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: mock the .class mtime + server start time and assert the staleness predicate fires correctly (fresh server → reuse; older server → restart; no server → start). 2. Integration: start voyage-batch with no automation server — assert one comes up and /health returns 200. 3. Integration: touch a .java file, recompile, start voyage-batch with the old server running — assert it's killed and replaced. 4. Live smoke: run /be-voyage-agent for skull against a freshly-started server and verify validate_dsl reflects a post-rename port name immediately, with no manual server restart.
